perspectives.name: discovery-weak-signals

factors.name: supplyChainResilience
factors.basis: Nebius and Bloom Energy disclosed a long-term power partnership using behind-the-meter fuel cells, with 328 MW of installed capacity planned operational in 2026. This is source-addressed evidence of a concrete time-to-power strategy that reduces dependence on new transmission build for part of the U.S. expansion.

risks: A planned 328 MW deployment is not proof of commissioned capacity, sustained availability, delivered power cost, or economics at Nebius load factors.
Behind-the-meter generation diversifies one bottleneck but does not remove GPU, construction, interconnection, fuel-supply, commissioning, or customer-utilization execution risk.
unknowns: The announcement does not disclose project-level capex, power price, fuel contract terms, realized uptime, commissioning milestones, or the portion of Nebius contracted demand served by the 328 MW deployment.

perspectives.name: expectations-execution

factors.name: bottleneckControl
factors.basis: The disclosed Bloom deployment addresses the power-availability bottleneck with modular behind-the-meter generation and an explicit 2026 operating target, creating a measurable execution checkpoint rather than only a long-range capacity ambition.

risks: The operating target remains forward-looking until commissioning evidence confirms delivered capacity.
Fast time-to-power does not by itself establish attractive unit economics or full data-center readiness.
unknowns: No realized commissioning percentage, delivered MW, utilization, power cost, or financial return is disclosed in this source.

sources.origin: Nebius newsroom / joint Nebius-Bloom Energy announcement
facts: Nebius and Bloom Energy announced a long-term partnership to deploy Bloom fuel-cell systems for Nebius AI infrastructure.
The companies stated that 328 MW of installed capacity was planned to be operational in 2026.
The systems are designed to provide behind-the-meter electricity and reduce dependence on new transmission build, supporting faster time-to-power.

result: Materially different source-addressed power-delivery evidence packaged for Alpha. It improves supply-chain-resilience and bottleneck-control inputs while preserving the distinction between planned and commissioned capacity and does not create Alpha numeric underwriting.
